1.modern-en: Ten-year-old Jane lives as an unwanted dependent at Gateshead Hall. Bullied by her cousin John Reed, she fights back for the first time when he strikes her with a book. Mrs. Reed punishes her by ordering her locked in the red room.
1.modern-da: Den tiårige Jane bor som uønsket plejebarn på Gateshead Hall. Da hendes fætter John Reed slår hende med en bog, gør hun for første gang modstand. Mrs. Reed straffer hende ved at beordre hende låst inde i det røde værelse.

2.modern-en: Locked in the red room where her uncle died, Jane is terrified by a moving light she takes for a ghost. She screams in panic and faints. Reflects bitterly on the injustice of her treatment by the Reed family.
2.modern-da: Låst inde i det røde værelse, hvor hendes onkel døde, bliver Jane skræmt af et bevægeligt lys, som hun tror er et spøgelse. Hun skriger i panik og besvimer. Reflekterer bittert over den uretfærdige behandling fra familien Reed.

3.modern-en: Recovers from her collapse with the kindly apothecary Mr. Lloyd attending her. Confides her unhappiness to him. Overhears that her parents were poor and both died of typhus. Mr. Lloyd suggests she be sent to school.
3.modern-da: Kommer sig efter sit sammenbrud med den venlige apoteker Mr. Lloyd ved sin side. Betror ham sin ulykkelighed. Overhører, at hendes forældre var fattige og begge døde af tyfus. Mr. Lloyd foreslår, at hun sendes i skole.

4.modern-en: Confronts Mrs. Reed with surprising boldness, telling her that Uncle Reed would despise her treatment. Meets Mr. Brocklehurst, who interrogates her about her character. Mrs. Reed poisons his opinion of Jane. Jane defiantly tells Mrs. Reed she is deceitful and cruel.
4.modern-da: Konfronterer Mrs. Reed med overraskende dristighed og fortæller hende, at onkel Reed ville foragte hendes behandling. Møder Mr. Brocklehurst, der udspørger hende om hendes karakter. Mrs. Reed forgifter hans opfattelse af Jane. Jane fortæller trodsigt Mrs. Reed, at hun er falsk og grusom.

5.modern-en: Arrives at Lowood Institution after a long, cold journey. Finds the school austere and the food terrible. Meets Helen Burns, who is reading a book by the fire, and is immediately drawn to her.
5.modern-da: Ankommer til Lowood efter en lang, kold rejse. Finder skolen streng og maden forfærdelig. Møder Helen Burns, der sidder og læser ved kaminen, og føler sig straks draget mod hende.

6.modern-en: Watches Helen Burns endure unjust punishment from Miss Scatcherd with astonishing patience. They have a deep conversation about forgiveness, love of enemies, and Christian endurance. Jane declares she cannot forgive those who wrong her.
6.modern-da: Ser Helen Burns udholde uretfærdig straf fra Miss Scatcherd med forbløffende tålmodighed. De fører en dyb samtale om tilgivelse, fjendekærlighed og kristen udholdenhed. Jane erklærer, at hun ikke kan tilgive dem, der gør hende uret.

7.modern-en: Endures the harsh winter conditions at Lowood. Mr. Brocklehurst visits and publicly humiliates her, making her stand on a stool and declaring her a liar. Helen Burns passes by and gives her a comforting look.
7.modern-da: Udholder de barske vinterforhold på Lowood. Mr. Brocklehurst besøger skolen og ydmyger hende offentligt ved at stille hende op på en skammel og erklære hende for en løgner. Helen Burns går forbi og sender hende et trøstende blik.

8.modern-en: Devastated by the public humiliation. Helen Burns and Miss Temple comfort her. Miss Temple invites them to tea and listens to Jane's account of her life at Gateshead. Miss Temple writes to Mr. Lloyd, who confirms Jane's story, and Jane is publicly cleared.
8.modern-da: Er knust efter den offentlige ydmygelse. Helen Burns og Miss Temple trøster hende. Miss Temple inviterer dem til te og lytter til Janes beretning om sit liv på Gateshead. Miss Temple skriver til Mr. Lloyd, der bekræfter Janes historie, og Jane bliver offentligt renset.

9.modern-en: Spring brings typhus to Lowood, killing many students. While the epidemic rages, Jane enjoys a strange freedom outdoors. Learns that Helen Burns is dying of consumption. Sneaks into Helen's bed at night to hold her; wakes to find Helen has died in her arms.
9.modern-da: Foråret bringer tyfus til Lowood og dræber mange elever. Mens epidemien raser, nyder Jane en mærkelig frihed udendørs. Hører, at Helen Burns er ved at dø af tuberkulose. Sniger sig ind i Helens seng om natten for at holde om hende; vågner og opdager, at Helen er død i hendes arme.

10.modern-en: Eight years pass at Lowood — six as student, two as teacher. After Miss Temple marries and leaves, Jane feels restless. She advertises for a governess position and receives an offer from Thornfield Hall. Bessie visits and tells her about the Reeds' decline.
10.modern-da: Otte år går på Lowood — seks som elev, to som lærer. Da Miss Temple gifter sig og rejser, føler Jane sig rastløs. Hun annoncerer efter en guvernantestilling og modtager et tilbud fra Thornfield Hall. Bessie besøger hende og fortæller om familien Reeds forfald.

11.modern-en: Arrives at Thornfield Hall and meets the kindly housekeeper Mrs. Fairfax and her pupil Adèle Varens. Tours the grand but gloomy house. On the third floor, hears a strange, disturbing laugh — attributed to the servant Grace Poole.
11.modern-da: Ankommer til Thornfield Hall og møder den venlige husbestyrerinde Mrs. Fairfax og sin elev Adèle Varens. Får en rundvisning i det storslåede, men dystre hus. På tredje sal hører hun en mærkelig, foruroligende latter — tilskrevet tjenestepigen Grace Poole.

12.modern-en: Settles into her routine at Thornfield but feels restless, longing for more experience. On a winter walk to post a letter, meets Mr. Rochester for the first time when his horse slips on ice. Helps him without knowing who he is.
12.modern-da: Falder til ro i sin hverdag på Thornfield, men føler sig rastløs og længes efter mere af livet. På en vintervandring for at poste et brev møder hun Mr. Rochester for første gang, da hans hest glider på isen. Hjælper ham uden at vide, hvem han er.

13.modern-en: Formally meets Rochester as master of Thornfield. He examines her paintings and questions her about her life, education, and skills. Finds him brusque but fascinating. Mrs. Fairfax explains his difficult family history.
13.modern-da: Møder formelt Rochester som herre til Thornfield. Han ser på hendes malerier og udspørger hende om hendes liv, uddannelse og evner. Finder ham brysk, men fascinerende. Mrs. Fairfax forklarer hans vanskelige familiehistorie.

14.modern-en: Has a long evening conversation with Rochester about morality, sin, and redemption. He hints at past mistakes and a desire to reform. Jane boldly tells him that wrongdoing cannot be undone by further error. Their intellectual connection deepens.
14.modern-da: Fører en lang aftensamtale med Rochester om moral, synd og forløsning. Han antyder tidligere fejltrin og et ønske om at reformere sig. Jane fortæller ham dristigt, at uret ikke kan gøres god igen med yderligere fejl. Deres intellektuelle forbindelse uddybes.

15.modern-en: Learns from Rochester that Adèle is the daughter of a French opera dancer who claimed Rochester was the father. Wakes in the night to find Rochester's bed curtains on fire. Rushes in and saves his life by dousing the flames. He holds her hand with deep gratitude.
15.modern-da: Hører fra Rochester, at Adèle er datter af en fransk operadanserinde, der hævdede, Rochester var faderen. Vågner om natten og finder Rochesters sengeforhæng i brand. Styrter ind og redder hans liv ved at slukke flammerne. Han holder hendes hånd med dyb taknemmelighed.

16.modern-en: The fire is blamed on Grace Poole, who remains employed — puzzling Jane. Rochester leaves suddenly for a house party. Mrs. Fairfax describes the beautiful Blanche Ingram. Jane paints contrasting portraits of herself and Blanche to discipline her feelings.
16.modern-da: Branden tilskrives Grace Poole, der forbliver ansat — til Janes forundring. Rochester rejser pludseligt til et selskab. Mrs. Fairfax beskriver den smukke Blanche Ingram. Jane maler kontrasterende portrætter af sig selv og Blanche for at disciplinere sine følelser.

17.modern-en: Rochester returns with a grand house party including Blanche Ingram. Jane observes from the shadows as Blanche flirts openly with Rochester. Overhears the Ingrams mocking governesses. Rochester ignores Jane all evening, deepening her pain.
17.modern-da: Rochester vender tilbage med et stort selskab, heriblandt Blanche Ingram. Jane observerer fra skyggerne, mens Blanche åbenlyst flirter med Rochester. Overhører Ingram-familien gøre nar af guvernanter. Rochester ignorerer Jane hele aftenen, hvilket uddyber hendes smerte.

18.modern-en: The house party continues with charades. Blanche and Rochester act out a bridal scene together. Jane watches with quiet anguish, convinced Rochester will marry Blanche despite sensing his indifference toward her. A mysterious stranger named Mr. Mason arrives.
18.modern-da: Selskabet fortsætter med pantomime. Blanche og Rochester opfører en brudescene sammen. Jane ser til med stille kval, overbevist om at Rochester vil gifte sig med Blanche, trods hans tilsyneladende ligegyldighed over for hende. En mystisk fremmed ved navn Mr. Mason ankommer.

19.modern-en: A gypsy fortune-teller (actually Rochester in disguise) questions Jane about her feelings, probing whether she cares for Rochester. Jane is guarded but reveals more than she intends. When Rochester drops the disguise, Jane tells him Mason has arrived — Rochester turns pale.
19.modern-da: En sigøjnerspåkone (i virkeligheden Rochester i forklædning) udspørger Jane om hendes følelser og prøver at afdække, om hun holder af Rochester. Jane er på vagt, men afslører mere end tilsigtet. Da Rochester afslører forklædningen, fortæller Jane ham, at Mason er ankommet — Rochester blegner.

20.modern-en: Woken in the night by a scream. Rochester asks her to help tend the wounded Mason, who has been stabbed and bitten. Jane nurses Mason in a terrifying vigil, forbidden to speak to him. Rochester sends Mason away at dawn. Jane senses deep secrets being concealed.
20.modern-da: Vækkes om natten af et skrig. Rochester beder hende hjælpe med at pleje den sårede Mason, der er blevet stukket og bidt. Jane plejer Mason under en skræmmende nattevagt, forbudt at tale med ham. Rochester sender Mason bort ved daggry. Jane fornemmer dybe hemmeligheder, der skjules.

21.modern-en: Summoned to Gateshead where Mrs. Reed is dying. Reconciles with the now-grown Eliza and Georgiana. Mrs. Reed confesses on her deathbed that she told Jane's uncle John Eyre that Jane was dead, out of spite. Jane forgives her. Mrs. Reed dies unreconciled.
21.modern-da: Tilkaldes til Gateshead, hvor Mrs. Reed ligger for døden. Forsones med de nu voksne Eliza og Georgiana. Mrs. Reed tilstår på sit dødsleje, at hun af ondskab fortalte Janes onkel John Eyre, at Jane var død. Jane tilgiver hende. Mrs. Reed dør uforsonet.

22.modern-en: Returns to Thornfield after a month away. Learns Rochester is expected back. Her heart leaps when she sees him in the orchard. He greets her warmly, calling Thornfield her home. Jane realizes the depth of her love for him.
22.modern-da: Vender tilbage til Thornfield efter en måneds fravær. Hører, at Rochester ventes hjem. Hendes hjerte springer, da hun ser ham i frugthaven. Han hilser hende varmt og kalder Thornfield hendes hjem. Jane indser dybden af sin kærlighed til ham.

23.modern-en: In the garden at midsummer, Rochester tells Jane she must leave because he is to marry Blanche. Jane breaks down, declaring her love and her equality of spirit. Rochester reveals it was all a test — he loves Jane, not Blanche — and proposes. Jane accepts. A storm splits the chestnut tree.
23.modern-da: I haven ved midsommer fortæller Rochester Jane, at hun må rejse, fordi han skal giftes med Blanche. Jane bryder sammen og erklærer sin kærlighed og sin åndelige ligestilling. Rochester afslører, at det var en prøve — han elsker Jane, ikke Blanche — og frier. Jane accepterer. En storm kløver kastanjetræet.

24.modern-en: Preparations for the wedding. Jane resists Rochester's attempts to dress her lavishly, insisting on her independence. She writes to her uncle John Eyre in Madeira. Feels uneasy, sensing Rochester's possessiveness and her own vulnerability.
24.modern-da: Forberedelser til brylluppet. Jane modstår Rochesters forsøg på at klæde hende overdådigt på og insisterer på sin uafhængighed. Hun skriver til sin onkel John Eyre på Madeira. Føler sig urolig og fornemmer Rochesters besiddertrang og sin egen sårbarhed.

25.modern-en: The night before the wedding, Jane is troubled by dark omens: the chestnut tree has been split by lightning. In the night, a terrifying figure — tall, dark-haired, savage — enters her room, tries on her wedding veil, rips it in two, and looms over her. Rochester claims it was Grace Poole.
25.modern-da: Natten før brylluppet er Jane plaget af mørke varsler: kastanjetræet er kløvet af lynet. Om natten trænger en skræmmende skikkelse — høj, mørkhåret, vild — ind i hendes værelse, prøver hendes brudeslør, river det i to stykker og bøjer sig truende over hende. Rochester hævder, det var Grace Poole.

26.modern-en: At the altar, a solicitor halts the ceremony, declaring Rochester already has a living wife. Mason confirms it. Rochester takes everyone to the third floor to see Bertha Mason, his insane wife. Jane's world collapses. She retreats to her room in shock.
26.modern-da: Ved alteret standser en advokat ceremonien og erklærer, at Rochester allerede har en levende hustru. Mason bekræfter det. Rochester tager alle med op på tredje sal for at se Bertha Mason, hans sindssyge hustru. Janes verden bryder sammen. Hun trækker sig tilbage til sit værelse i chok.

27.modern-en: Rochester tells Jane his full story: his forced marriage to Bertha in Jamaica, her hereditary madness, his years of misery. He begs Jane to live with him in France. Jane refuses despite her love — she will not be his mistress. She flees Thornfield at dawn.
27.modern-da: Rochester fortæller Jane hele sin historie: sit tvungne ægteskab med Bertha i Jamaica, hendes arvelige sindssyge, hans år i elendighed. Han bønfalder Jane om at leve med ham i Frankrig. Jane nægter trods sin kærlighed — hun vil ikke være hans elskerinde. Hun flygter fra Thornfield ved daggry.

28.modern-en: Wanders penniless on the moors for three days, begging for food and sleeping outdoors. Nearly dies of exposure and hunger. Collapses on the doorstep of Moor House, where she is taken in by the Rivers siblings after St. John overrules the servant who would turn her away.
28.modern-da: Vandrer pengeløs på heden i tre dage, tigger om mad og sover udendørs. Er tæt på at dø af udmattelse og sult. Bryder sammen på trappen til Moor House, hvor hun tages ind af søskendeparret Rivers, efter St. John tilsidesætter tjenestepigen, der ville afvise hende.

29.modern-en: Recovers at Moor House over several days, nursed by the Rivers sisters Diana and Mary. Gives her name as Jane Elliott to conceal her identity. St. John questions her closely but respects her privacy. Jane asks only for honest work.
29.modern-da: Kommer sig på Moor House over flere dage, plejet af Rivers-søstrene Diana og Mary. Opgiver sit navn som Jane Elliott for at skjule sin identitet. St. John udspørger hende indgående, men respekterer hendes privatliv. Jane beder kun om ærligt arbejde.

30.modern-en: Settles at Moor House and bonds with Diana and Mary over shared intellectual interests. Learns the Rivers family has suffered financial loss. St. John offers Jane a position as teacher at the village school in Morton.
30.modern-da: Slår sig ned på Moor House og knytter bånd til Diana og Mary gennem fælles intellektuelle interesser. Hører, at familien Rivers har lidt et økonomisk tab. St. John tilbyder Jane en stilling som lærerinde på landsbyskolen i Morton.

31.modern-en: Takes up her position as schoolmistress in Morton. Feels humbled but determined. St. John visits and tells her about his own struggles between ambition and duty. Rosamond Oliver, the beautiful daughter of a local benefactor, arrives — clearly smitten with St. John.
31.modern-da: Tiltræder sin stilling som skolelærerinde i Morton. Føler sig ydmyget, men er beslutsom. St. John besøger hende og fortæller om sine egne kampe mellem ambition og pligt. Rosamond Oliver, den smukke datter af en lokal velgører, ankommer — tydeligt betaget af St. John.

32.modern-en: Grows fond of her students and earns the village's respect. Paints a portrait of Rosamond Oliver and confronts St. John about his feelings for her. He admits he loves Rosamond but insists she would not suit a missionary's life. He abruptly tears a strip from Jane's paper — she doesn't know why.
32.modern-da: Vokser sig glad for sine elever og vinder landsbyens respekt. Maler et portræt af Rosamond Oliver og konfronterer St. John med hans følelser for hende. Han indrømmer, at han elsker Rosamond, men insisterer på, at hun ikke passer til et missionærliv. Han river brat en strimmel af Janes papir — hun ved ikke hvorfor.

33.modern-en: St. John reveals he tore the paper because it bore the name 'Jane Eyre.' He has discovered her identity and that her uncle John Eyre has died, leaving her a fortune of twenty thousand pounds. He also reveals that John Eyre was the Rivers' uncle too — they are cousins. Jane insists on dividing the inheritance equally.
33.modern-da: St. John afslører, at han rev papiret, fordi der stod 'Jane Eyre' på det. Han har opdaget hendes identitet, og at hendes onkel John Eyre er død og har efterladt hende en formue på tyve tusind pund. Han afslører også, at John Eyre var Rivers-familien onkel — de er fætre og kusiner. Jane insisterer på at dele arven ligeligt.

34.modern-en: Uses her inheritance to renovate Moor House for the returning Diana and Mary. St. John begins pressuring Jane to learn Hindustani and join him as a missionary wife in India. She resists, willing to go as a fellow worker but refusing to marry without love.
34.modern-da: Bruger sin arv til at renovere Moor House til Diana og Marys hjemkomst. St. John begynder at presse Jane til at lære hindustani og følge ham som missionærhustru til Indien. Hun gør modstand — villig til at rejse som medarbejder, men nægter at gifte sig uden kærlighed.

35.modern-en: St. John intensifies his campaign, using religious duty and emotional manipulation. Jane nearly yields under his iron will. At the crucial moment, she hears Rochester's voice calling her name across the moors — 'Jane! Jane! Jane!' She answers 'I am coming!' and breaks free of St. John's influence.
35.modern-da: St. John intensiverer sin kampagne med religiøs pligt og følelsesmæssig manipulation. Jane er tæt på at give efter under hans jernvilje. I det afgørende øjeblik hører hun Rochesters stemme kalde hendes navn hen over heden — 'Jane! Jane! Jane!' Hun svarer 'Jeg kommer!' og bryder fri af St. Johns indflydelse.

36.modern-en: Travels to Thornfield and discovers it has burned to a blackened ruin. Learns from the innkeeper that Bertha set the fire and leapt to her death from the roof. Rochester tried to save her and was blinded and lost a hand. He now lives at the remote Ferndean manor.
36.modern-da: Rejser til Thornfield og opdager, at det er brændt ned til en sværtet ruin. Hører fra kromanden, at Bertha startede branden og sprang i døden fra taget. Rochester forsøgte at redde hende og blev blindet og mistede en hånd. Han bor nu på det afsides Ferndean.

37.modern-en: Finds Rochester at Ferndean, blind and maimed. He cannot believe she is real. She tells him she is independent and wealthy. He proposes again and she accepts. They discover both heard the supernatural voice calling across the distance on the same night.
37.modern-da: Finder Rochester på Ferndean, blind og lemlæstet. Han kan ikke tro, hun er virkelig. Hun fortæller ham, at hun er uafhængig og velhavende. Han frier igen, og hun accepterer. De opdager, at de begge hørte den overnaturlige stemme kalde over afstanden samme nat.

38.modern-en: Marries Rochester in a quiet ceremony. Reports ten years of perfect happiness. Rochester regains partial sight in one eye after two years — enough to see their firstborn son. Diana and Mary marry well. St. John goes to India as a missionary and faces a heroic death.
38.modern-da: Gifter sig med Rochester i en stille ceremoni. Beretter om ti års fuldkommen lykke. Rochester genvinder delvist synet på det ene øje efter to år — nok til at se deres førstefødte søn. Diana og Mary gifter sig godt. St. John rejser til Indien som missionær og møder en heroisk død.

12.modern-en: Meets Jane for the first time on the road to Hay when his horse slips on ice. She helps him remount without knowing he is her employer. Arrives at Thornfield, sending Adèle into raptures with gifts.
12.modern-da: Møder Jane for første gang på vejen til Hay, da hans hest glider på isen. Hun hjælper ham op uden at vide, at han er hendes arbejdsgiver. Ankommer til Thornfield og henrykker Adèle med gaver.

13.modern-en: Summons Jane and Adèle to the drawing room. Examines Jane's paintings with intense interest, questioning her about their strange, visionary subjects. Gruff and commanding, yet clearly intrigued by her mind.
13.modern-da: Tilkalder Jane og Adèle i dagligstuen. Studerer Janes malerier med intens interesse og udspørger hende om deres mærkelige, visionære motiver. Brysk og bydende, men tydeligt fascineret af hendes sind.

14.modern-en: Opens up to Jane about his past sins and desire for moral reform. Speaks of seeking redemption through a new connection. Hints darkly at being trapped by circumstances. Their unequal positions begin to dissolve in genuine intellectual exchange.
14.modern-da: Åbner sig for Jane om sine tidligere synder og sit ønske om moralsk reform. Taler om at søge forløsning gennem en ny forbindelse. Antyder mørkt, at han er fanget af omstændighederne. Deres ulige positioner begynder at opløses i ægte intellektuel udveksling.

15.modern-en: Tells Jane about Céline Varens, Adèle's mother, and his disillusionment with love. Nearly dies when his bed curtains catch fire in the night. Jane saves him. Grips her hand with intense emotion and thanks her as if his life depended on it — which it did.
15.modern-da: Fortæller Jane om Céline Varens, Adèles mor, og sin desillusion med kærlighed. Er tæt på at dø, da hans sengeforhæng bryder i brand om natten. Jane redder ham. Griber hendes hånd med intens følelse og takker hende, som om hans liv afhang af det — hvilket det gjorde.

16.modern-en: Departs suddenly for a house party. Jane hears from Mrs. Fairfax about the beautiful Blanche Ingram and suspects Rochester's interest in her.
16.modern-da: Rejser pludseligt til et selskab. Jane hører fra Mrs. Fairfax om den smukke Blanche Ingram og mistænker Rochesters interesse for hende.

17.modern-en: Returns with a grand party of guests, including Blanche Ingram. Appears to court Blanche while ignoring Jane entirely. Yet when their eyes briefly meet across the room, Jane senses his unchanged feelings.
17.modern-da: Vender tilbage med et stort selskab af gæster, heriblandt Blanche Ingram. Synes at bejle til Blanche, mens han fuldstændigt ignorerer Jane. Men da deres øjne kort mødes på tværs af rummet, fornemmer Jane hans uændrede følelser.

18.modern-en: Performs in charades with Blanche, acting out a bridal scene. Appears visibly disturbed when the stranger Mr. Mason arrives, turning pale and clutching a wine glass for support.
18.modern-da: Optræder i pantomime med Blanche og opfører en brudescene. Bliver synligt forstyrret, da den fremmede Mr. Mason ankommer, blegner og griber fat i et vinglas for støtte.

19.modern-en: Disguises himself as a gypsy fortune-teller to probe Jane's feelings. Drops the disguise after learning she has kept her emotions carefully hidden. His mood darkens sharply when Jane mentions Mason's arrival.
19.modern-da: Forklæder sig som sigøjnerspåkone for at udforske Janes følelser. Afslører sig selv, efter han har erfaret, at hun har holdt sine følelser omhyggeligt skjult. Hans humør mørknes kraftigt, da Jane nævner Masons ankomst.

20.modern-en: After Mason is attacked in the night, Rochester enlists Jane to nurse him. Manages the crisis with calm authority while keeping the truth hidden. Sends Mason away at dawn, extracting a promise of silence. In the garden afterward, speaks wistfully of seeking forgiveness and a fresh start.
20.modern-da: Efter Mason angribes om natten, får Rochester Jane til at pleje ham. Håndterer krisen med rolig autoritet, mens han holder sandheden skjult. Sender Mason bort ved daggry og aftvinger ham et løfte om tavshed. I haven bagefter taler han vemodig om at søge tilgivelse og en ny begyndelse.

23.modern-en: Tests Jane by telling her she must leave because he will marry Blanche. When Jane passionately declares her love and spiritual equality, he reveals it was all a ruse and proposes. Overcome with joy and urgency, as if fearful the moment will slip away.
23.modern-da: Prøver Jane ved at fortælle hende, at hun må rejse, fordi han vil gifte sig med Blanche. Da Jane lidenskabeligt erklærer sin kærlighed og åndelige ligestilling, afslører han, at det var en list, og frier. Overvældet af glæde og hast, som frygtede han, at øjeblikket skulle glide bort.

24.modern-en: Showers Jane with gifts and attention during the engagement, trying to dress her like a queen. Jane resists, maintaining her independence. He is possessive and adoring, calling her his 'elf' and 'fairy.'
24.modern-da: Overøser Jane med gaver og opmærksomhed under forlovelsen og forsøger at klæde hende som en dronning. Jane gør modstand og fastholder sin uafhængighed. Han er besiddende og tilbedende og kalder hende sin 'alf' og 'fe.'

25.modern-en: Returns from a trip to find Jane shaken by a nightmare intruder who tore her veil. Dismisses it as Grace Poole's doing. Holds Jane close, desperate to reassure her on the eve of their wedding.
25.modern-da: Vender hjem fra en rejse og finder Jane rystet af en ubuden nattegæst, der rev hendes slør i stykker. Afviser det som Grace Pooles værk. Holder Jane tæt, desperat efter at berolige hende aftenen før deres bryllup.

26.modern-en: Stands at the altar as the wedding is halted. His secret is exposed: he is already married to Bertha Mason. Takes the entire party to the third floor to see his insane wife, presenting his tormented defense. His bigamy attempt has failed.
26.modern-da: Står ved alteret, da brylluppet standses. Hans hemmelighed afsløres: han er allerede gift med Bertha Mason. Fører hele selskabet op på tredje sal for at se sin sindssyge hustru og fremlægger sit plagede forsvar. Hans bigamiforsøg er mislykket.

27.modern-en: Pours out the full story of his disastrous marriage to Bertha, arranged by his father for money. Tells of her madness, his despair, and his decade of wandering. Begs Jane to come to France as his companion. She refuses and he is devastated. Wakes to find she has fled.
27.modern-da: Fortæller hele historien om sit katastrofale ægteskab med Bertha, arrangeret af hans far for penge. Beretter om hendes sindssyge, sin fortvivlelse og sit årti af omflakken. Bønfalder Jane om at tage med til Frankrig. Hun nægter, og han er knust. Vågner og opdager, at hun er flygtet.

36.modern-en: Described by the innkeeper: after Jane's departure, Rochester became a recluse, wandering Thornfield like a ghost. When Bertha set the fire, he heroically evacuated all the servants and tried to save her from the roof. Lost his sight and a hand in the collapse. Now lives alone at Ferndean.
36.modern-da: Beskrevet af kromanden: efter Janes afrejse blev Rochester en eneboer, der vandrede rundt på Thornfield som et spøgelse. Da Bertha startede branden, evakuerede han heroisk alle tjenestefolkene og forsøgte at redde hende fra taget. Mistede sit syn og en hånd i sammenstyrtningen. Bor nu alene på Ferndean.

37.modern-en: Living blind and broken at Ferndean. When Jane appears, he cannot believe she is real, fearing she is a ghost or dream. Learns she is wealthy and independent. Proposes again with humility. Confesses he cried out her name in despair — the same night she heard his voice across the moors. Prays in gratitude to God.
37.modern-da: Lever blind og nedbrudt på Ferndean. Da Jane dukker op, kan han ikke tro, hun er virkelig, og frygter, hun er et spøgelse eller en drøm. Hører, at hun er velhavende og uafhængig. Frier igen med ydmyghed. Tilstår, at han råbte hendes navn i fortvivlelse — samme nat som hun hørte hans stemme over heden. Beder i taknemmelighed til Gud.

38.modern-en: Marries Jane quietly. After two years of blindness, partially regains sight in one eye — enough to see their firstborn son. Lives ten years of deep, inseparable happiness with Jane, grateful for mercy after judgment.
38.modern-da: Gifter sig med Jane i stilhed. Efter to års blindhed genvinder han delvist synet på det ene øje — nok til at se deres førstefødte søn. Lever ti år i dyb, uadskillelig lykke med Jane, taknemmelig for nåde efter dom.

epithet.en: Jane's aunt and guardian at Gateshead
epithet.da: Janes tante og værge på Gateshead

1.modern-en: Excludes Jane from the family circle, claiming she is not a pleasant, well-behaved child. When Jane fights back against John, Mrs. Reed orders her locked in the red room as punishment.
1.modern-da: Udelukker Jane fra familiekredsen med den begrundelse, at hun ikke er et behageligt, velopdraget barn. Da Jane slår igen mod John, beordrer Mrs. Reed hende låst inde i det røde værelse som straf.

2.modern-en: Ignores Jane's terrified screams from the red room. Accuses her of manipulating and performing. Shoves her back in and locks the door despite Jane's desperate pleas.
2.modern-da: Ignorerer Janes rædselsskreg fra det røde værelse. Anklager hende for at manipulere og spille teater. Skubber hende tilbage og låser døren trods Janes desperate bønner.

3.modern-en: Mentioned in servants' gossip as having been too hard on Jane. The apothecary Mr. Lloyd recommends Jane be sent away to school — a suggestion Mrs. Reed eagerly accepts.
3.modern-da: Nævnes i tjenestefolkenes sladder som havende været for hård mod Jane. Apotekeren Mr. Lloyd anbefaler, at Jane sendes på kostskole — et forslag Mrs. Reed ivrigt accepterer.

4.modern-en: Introduces Jane to Mr. Brocklehurst and poisons his opinion by calling Jane deceitful. Jane retaliates with a furious speech accusing Mrs. Reed of cruelty. Mrs. Reed is visibly shaken, unable to comprehend the child's defiance.
4.modern-da: Præsenterer Jane for Mr. Brocklehurst og forgifter hans opfattelse ved at kalde Jane bedragerisk. Jane gengælder med en rasende tale, der anklager Mrs. Reed for grusomhed. Mrs. Reed er synligt rystet og ude af stand til at forstå barnets trods.

21.modern-en: Lies dying at Gateshead, broken by trouble and family dysfunction. Confesses to Jane that she wrote to Jane's uncle John Eyre claiming Jane was dead — a deliberate act of spite to prevent Jane's adoption and prosperity. Dies without truly forgiving or accepting Jane.
21.modern-da: Ligger for døden på Gateshead, nedbrudt af problemer og familiens dysfunktion. Tilstår over for Jane, at hun skrev til Janes onkel John Eyre og hævdede, Jane var død — en bevidst ondskabsfuld handling for at forhindre Janes adoption og velstand. Dør uden virkelig at tilgive eller acceptere Jane.

1.modern-en: A spoiled, overweight fourteen-year-old who bullies Jane relentlessly. Finds her reading behind a curtain, lectures her about being a dependent, and hurls a book at her head. When she fights back, he screams for his mother.
1.modern-da: En forkælet, overvægtig fjortenårig, der ubarmhjertigt tyranniserer Jane. Finder hende læsende bag et gardin, belærer hende om at være plejebarn og kaster en bog i hovedet på hende. Da hun slår igen, skriger han på sin mor.

4.modern-en: Tries to hit Jane again but she turns on him fiercely, and he retreats in fear. His mother tells him to stay away from Jane entirely.
4.modern-da: Forsøger at slå Jane igen, men hun vender sig voldsomt mod ham, og han trækker sig tilbage i frygt. Hans mor fortæller ham at holde sig helt væk fra Jane.

21.modern-en: Mentioned as having gone to ruin: he dissipated his fortune, lived wildly, and is rumored to have died by suicide. His decline is one of the causes of Mrs. Reed's fatal illness.
21.modern-da: Nævnes som havende ødelagt sig selv: han ødslede sin formue, levede vildt og siges at have begået selvmord. Hans forfald er en af årsagerne til Mrs. Reeds dødelige sygdom.

5.modern-en: First seen sitting by the fire reading Rasselas. Jane is drawn to her calm, intelligent presence amid the bleakness of Lowood. They share a brief but warm first conversation.
5.modern-da: Ses første gang siddende ved ilden og læse Rasselas. Jane drages mod hendes rolige, intelligente væsen midt i Lowoods trøstesløshed. De deler en kort, men varm første samtale.

6.modern-en: Endures humiliation from Miss Scatcherd with bewildering patience. In a long philosophical conversation with Jane, advocates Christian forgiveness and love of enemies. Speaks of eternity and the soul with visionary conviction.
6.modern-da: Udholder ydmygelse fra Miss Scatcherd med forbavsende tålmodighed. I en lang filosofisk samtale med Jane går hun ind for kristen tilgivelse og fjendekærlighed. Taler om evigheden og sjælen med visionær overbevisning.

7.modern-en: Passes by Jane during her public humiliation on the stool and gives her a look of courage and comfort that sustains her through the ordeal.
7.modern-da: Går forbi Jane under hendes offentlige ydmygelse på skamlen og sender hende et blik fuldt af mod og trøst, der holder hende oppe gennem prøvelsen.

8.modern-en: Comes to comfort Jane after the humiliation, bringing her food and tea with Miss Temple. Engages in a brilliant conversation about history and literature. Her intellectual gifts and spiritual depth are fully displayed.
8.modern-da: Kommer for at trøste Jane efter ydmygelsen og bringer hende mad og te hos Miss Temple. Fører en brillant samtale om historie og litteratur. Hendes intellektuelle begavelse og åndelige dybde udfoldes fuldt ud.

9.modern-en: Dying of consumption while the typhus epidemic rages around her. Jane sneaks to her bed at night. Helen speaks of going home to God with serene faith. Dies in Jane's arms during the night — Jane wakes to find her friend gone.
9.modern-da: Dør af tuberkulose, mens tyfusepidemien raser omkring hende. Jane sniger sig til hendes seng om natten. Helen taler om at komme hjem til Gud med fredfyldt tro. Dør i Janes arme i løbet af natten — Jane vågner og finder sin veninde borte.

epithet.en: Clergyman and treasurer of Lowood Institution

4.modern-en: Visits Gateshead to interview Jane for admission to Lowood. A tall, grim, black-clad figure. Warns Jane about hell and deceit. Mrs. Reed tells him Jane is a liar, and he promises to alert the teachers.
4.modern-da: Besøger Gateshead for at interviewe Jane til optagelse på Lowood. En høj, barsk, sortklædt skikkelse. Advarer Jane om helvede og bedrag. Mrs. Reed fortæller ham, at Jane er en løgner, og han lover at advare lærerne.

7.modern-en: Visits Lowood and harangues Miss Temple about economy, forbidding extra food for starving students while his own daughters wear expensive furs. Publicly humiliates Jane by making her stand on a stool and declaring her a liar before the whole school.
7.modern-da: Besøger Lowood og holder Miss Temple en lang prædiken om sparsommelighed, forbyder ekstra mad til sultende elever, mens hans egne døtre bærer dyre pelse. Ydmyger Jane offentligt ved at stille hende op på en skammel og erklære hende for løgner foran hele skolen.

epithet.en: Rochester's first wife, imprisoned in Thornfield
epithet.da: Rochesters første hustru, indespærret på Thornfield

11.modern-en: Her unseen presence manifests as a strange, eerie laugh echoing through the third-floor corridor. Mrs. Fairfax attributes it to the servant Grace Poole.
11.modern-da: Hendes usynlige tilstedeværelse manifesterer sig som en mærkelig, uhyggelig latter, der genlyder i tredje sals korridor. Mrs. Fairfax tilskriver den tjenestepigen Grace Poole.

15.modern-en: Sets fire to Rochester's bed curtains in the night, nearly killing him. Jane extinguishes the flames and saves his life. The attack is attributed to Grace Poole.
15.modern-da: Sætter ild til Rochesters sengeforhæng om natten og er tæt på at dræbe ham. Jane slukker flammerne og redder hans liv. Angrebet tilskrives Grace Poole.

20.modern-en: Attacks her brother Richard Mason in the third-floor room, stabbing and biting him. Her savage violence is heard throughout the house but the truth is concealed from the guests.
20.modern-da: Angriber sin bror Richard Mason i tredje sals værelse, stikker og bider ham. Hendes vilde vold høres over hele huset, men sandheden skjules for gæsterne.

25.modern-en: Enters Jane's room the night before the wedding. Tries on Jane's wedding veil, looks at herself in the mirror, then rips the veil in two. Looms over the sleeping Jane with a savage face before withdrawing.
25.modern-da: Trænger ind i Janes værelse natten før brylluppet. Prøver Janes brudeslør, ser på sig selv i spejlet og river derefter sløret i to stykker. Bøjer sig truende over den sovende Jane med et vildt ansigt, før hun trækker sig tilbage.

26.modern-en: Revealed to the world when Rochester takes the wedding party to her room. Described as a large, dark-haired creature groveling on all fours. Springs at Rochester and seizes his throat. Is bound to a chair after a violent struggle.
26.modern-da: Afsløres for verden, da Rochester fører bryllupsselskabet til hendes værelse. Beskrives som en stor, mørkhåret skabning, der kravler rundt på alle fire. Kaster sig over Rochester og griber hans hals. Bindes til en stol efter en voldsom kamp.

27.modern-en: Rochester tells her full backstory: a Jamaican Creole heiress from a family riddled with madness. Their marriage was arranged for money. Her violent insanity emerged within years, forcing Rochester to confine her at Thornfield under Grace Poole's care.
27.modern-da: Rochester fortæller hendes fulde baggrund: en jamaicansk kreolsk arving fra en familie hærget af sindssyge. Deres ægteskab var arrangeret for penge. Hendes voldelige sindssyge viste sig inden for få år, hvilket tvang Rochester til at indespærre hende på Thornfield under Grace Pooles opsyn.

36.modern-en: Sets fire to Thornfield for the last time. Climbs to the roof where she is seen waving her arms and shouting. When Rochester approaches to save her, she leaps from the battlements to her death.
36.modern-da: Sætter ild til Thornfield for sidste gang. Klatrer op på taget, hvor hun ses vinke med armene og råbe. Da Rochester nærmer sig for at redde hende, springer hun fra brystværnet i døden.

epithet.en: Clergyman, Jane's cousin, missionary to India
epithet.da: Præst, Janes fætter, missionær i Indien

28.modern-en: Overrules his servant Hannah and admits the starving, collapsed Jane into Moor House. Cold and analytical in manner, but acts decisively to save her life.
28.modern-da: Tilsidesætter sin tjener Hannah og lukker den sultende, sammensunkne Jane ind i Moor House. Kold og analytisk i sit væsen, men handler resolutt for at redde hendes liv.

29.modern-en: Questions Jane closely about her identity and circumstances as she recovers. Respects her evasions but studies her with penetrating intelligence. A handsome, marble-featured young clergyman with an iron will.
29.modern-da: Udspørger Jane indgående om hendes identitet og omstændigheder, mens hun kommer sig. Respekterer hendes undvigelser, men studerer hende med gennemtrængende intelligens. En smuk, marmortrækkende ung præst med en jernvilje.

30.modern-en: Offers Jane the position of schoolmistress at the Morton village school. Reveals his own restless ambition — he feels called to missionary work despite his comfortable parish. His sisters worry about his intensity.
30.modern-da: Tilbyder Jane stillingen som skolelærerinde på landsbyskolen i Morton. Afslører sin egen rastløse ambition — han føler sig kaldet til missionsarbejde trods sit komfortable sogn. Hans søstre bekymrer sig om hans intensitet.

31.modern-en: Visits Jane at her new school and speaks candidly about his struggles between worldly desire and divine calling. Rosamond Oliver arrives and he visibly struggles to control his feelings for her.
31.modern-da: Besøger Jane på hendes nye skole og taler åbenhjertigt om sine kampe mellem verdsligt begær og guddommelig kaldelse. Rosamond Oliver ankommer, og han kæmper synligt for at kontrollere sine følelser for hende.

32.modern-en: Jane confronts him about his feelings for Rosamond Oliver using her portrait. He admits his love but insists Rosamond would be unsuitable for a missionary's wife. Gives himself exactly fifteen minutes to indulge the fantasy, then resolutely shuts it down. Tears a strip from Jane's paper.
32.modern-da: Jane konfronterer ham med hans følelser for Rosamond Oliver ved hjælp af hendes portræt. Han indrømmer sin kærlighed, men insisterer på, at Rosamond ville være uegnet som missionærhustru. Giver sig selv præcis femten minutter til at hengive sig til fantasien og lukker den derefter resolut ned. River en strimmel af Janes papir.

33.modern-en: Reveals he discovered Jane's true identity from the torn paper bearing her name. Tells her that her uncle John Eyre has died, leaving her twenty thousand pounds. Reveals the Rivers are her cousins through the same uncle. Initially cold about the inheritance, but moved by Jane's joy at finding family.
33.modern-da: Afslører, at han opdagede Janes sande identitet fra den afrevne papirstrimmel med hendes navn. Fortæller hende, at hendes onkel John Eyre er død og har efterladt hende tyve tusind pund. Afslører, at Rivers-familien er hendes kusiner og fætre gennem samme onkel. Først kølig omkring arven, men bevæget af Janes glæde over at finde familie.

34.modern-en: Begins pressuring Jane to learn Hindustani and accompany him to India as his wife. His campaign is relentless, using guilt, duty, and religious authority. Jane offers to go as a fellow worker but refuses marriage without love. His proposal is a command, not a confession of love.
34.modern-da: Begynder at presse Jane til at lære hindustani og følge ham til Indien som hans hustru. Hans kampagne er ubarmhjertig og bruger skyld, pligt og religiøs autoritet. Jane tilbyder at rejse som medarbejder, men nægter ægteskab uden kærlighed. Hans frieri er en befaling, ikke en kærlighedserklæring.

35.modern-en: Makes his final, most powerful appeal, nearly bending Jane's will through sheer spiritual force. She is on the verge of yielding when Rochester's voice calls her name supernaturally. St. John's hold over her is broken. He departs for Cambridge the next morning.
35.modern-da: Fremsætter sin sidste, mest magtfulde appel og er tæt på at bøje Janes vilje med ren åndelig kraft. Hun er på nippet til at give efter, da Rochesters stemme kalder hendes navn overnaturligt. St. Johns greb om hende er brudt. Han rejser til Cambridge næste morgen.

38.modern-en: Has gone to India as a missionary. Lives a life of heroic, self-denying labor. Never marries. Jane's last letter from him suggests he is nearing death, anticipating his eternal reward with serene faith.
38.modern-da: Er rejst til Indien som missionær. Lever et liv i heroisk, selvfornægtende arbejde. Gifter sig aldrig. Janes sidste brev fra ham antyder, at han nærmer sig døden og ser frem til sin evige belønning med fredfyldt tro.

28.modern-en: Helps take in the starving Jane at Moor House, showing immediate compassion and warmth.
28.modern-da: Hjælper med at tage den sultende Jane ind i Moor House og viser øjeblikkelig medfølelse og varme.

29.modern-en: Nurses Jane back to health over several days. Strong, intelligent, and warm-hearted. Jane feels an instant kinship with her and Mary that she has never felt before.
29.modern-da: Plejer Jane tilbage til sundhed over flere dage. Stærk, intelligent og varmhjertet. Jane føler et øjeblikkeligt slægtskab med hende og Mary, som hun aldrig har følt før.

30.modern-en: Shares intellectual interests with Jane — they study German together. Must leave Moor House to work as a governess due to the family's financial difficulties. Parts reluctantly from Jane and Mary.
30.modern-da: Deler intellektuelle interesser med Jane — de studerer tysk sammen. Må forlade Moor House for at arbejde som guvernante på grund af familiens økonomiske vanskeligheder. Skilles modvilligt fra Jane og Mary.

34.modern-en: Returns to the renovated Moor House for Christmas, overjoyed at having a real home again thanks to Jane's generosity with the inheritance.
34.modern-da: Vender tilbage til det renoverede Moor House til jul, overlykkelig over at have et rigtigt hjem igen takket være Janes gavmildhed med arven.

35.modern-en: Opposes St. John's pressure on Jane to marry him, telling Jane plainly that it would kill her to go to India as his wife. Recognizes St. John's domineering nature.
35.modern-da: Modsætter sig St. Johns pres på Jane for at gifte sig med ham og fortæller Jane ligeud, at det ville dræbe hende at rejse til Indien som hans hustru. Gennemskuer St. Johns dominerende natur.

38.modern-en: Has married Captain Fitzjames. She and Mary visit Jane and Rochester once a year. Approved of Jane's marriage without reservation.
38.modern-da: Har giftet sig med kaptajn Fitzjames. Hun og Mary besøger Jane og Rochester en gang om året. Billigede Janes ægteskab uden forbehold.

28.modern-en: Present when Jane is taken in at Moor House. Gentler and quieter than Diana, but equally compassionate.
28.modern-da: Til stede, da Jane tages ind på Moor House. Blødere og mere stille end Diana, men lige så medfølende.

29.modern-en: Helps nurse Jane alongside Diana. Quieter but deeply kind. Jane feels an immediate bond with both sisters.
29.modern-da: Hjælper Diana med at pleje Jane. Mere stille, men dybt venlig. Jane føler et øjeblikkeligt bånd til begge søstre.

30.modern-en: Like Diana, must leave Moor House for governess work. Shares the sisters' intellectual curiosity and quiet strength.
30.modern-da: Ligesom Diana må hun forlade Moor House for guvernantearbejde. Deler søstrenes intellektuelle nysgerrighed og stille styrke.

38.modern-en: Has married Mr. Wharton, a clergyman. Visits Jane and Rochester annually with Diana.
38.modern-da: Har giftet sig med Mr. Wharton, en præst. Besøger Jane og Rochester årligt sammen med Diana.

11.modern-en: Jane's lively young pupil at Thornfield. A cheerful, spoiled French child who chatters in French and broken English. Delighted by gifts and pretty things. Mrs. Fairfax explains she is Rochester's ward.
11.modern-da: Janes livlige unge elev på Thornfield. Et muntert, forkælet fransk barn, der pludrer på fransk og gebrokkent engelsk. Begejstret for gaver og smukke ting. Mrs. Fairfax forklarer, at hun er Rochesters myndling.

15.modern-en: Rochester reveals Adèle's history: she is the daughter of Céline Varens, a French opera dancer and Rochester's former mistress. Rochester doubts she is his biological daughter but keeps her out of pity.
15.modern-da: Rochester afslører Adèles historie: hun er datter af Céline Varens, en fransk operadanserinde og Rochesters tidligere elskerinde. Rochester tvivler på, at hun er hans biologiske datter, men beholder hende af medlidenhed.

17.modern-en: Thrilled by the house party. Dresses up and mingles with the guests, charming the ladies with her French manners.
17.modern-da: Begejstret over selskabet. Klæder sig ud og blander sig med gæsterne og charmerer damerne med sine franske manerer.

24.modern-en: Excited by the wedding preparations. Jane treats her with affection, seeing her as the emblem of her own past — innocent and dependent.
24.modern-da: Begejstret over bryllupsf orberedelserne. Jane behandler hende med kærlighed og ser hende som et symbol på sin egen fortid — uskyldig og afhængig.

38.modern-en: After the wedding, Jane rescues her from a strict school where she is unhappy. Places her in a better one, where she thrives. Grows into a pleasant, faithful companion.
38.modern-da: Efter brylluppet redder Jane hende fra en streng skole, hvor hun er ulykkelig. Anbringer hende på en bedre, hvor hun trives. Vokser op til en behagelig, trofast ledsager.

11.modern-en: Warmly welcomes Jane to Thornfield. A kind, elderly widow who serves as housekeeper. Shows Jane around the house, including the eerie third floor. Attributes the strange laugh to Grace Poole.
11.modern-da: Byder Jane varmt velkommen til Thornfield. En venlig, ældre enke, der fungerer som husbestyrerinde. Viser Jane rundt i huset, inklusive den uhyggelige tredje sal. Tilskriver den mærkelige latter til Grace Poole.

13.modern-en: Explains Rochester's difficult family history — his father and brother conspired to keep the estate from him. Describes Rochester as respectable but somewhat unusual and difficult to read.
13.modern-da: Forklarer Rochesters vanskelige familiehistorie — hans far og bror sammensvor sig for at holde godset fra ham. Beskriver Rochester som respektabel, men noget usædvanlig og svær at gennemskue.

16.modern-en: Describes the beautiful Blanche Ingram to Jane, unwittingly inflicting pain. Speculates that Rochester will marry Blanche.
16.modern-da: Beskriver den smukke Blanche Ingram for Jane og påfører hende uforvarende smerte. Spekulerer i, at Rochester vil gifte sig med Blanche.

22.modern-en: Has written to Jane during her absence, reporting that the house party has dispersed and Rochester has gone to London — perhaps to buy a carriage for his wedding to Blanche.
22.modern-da: Har skrevet til Jane under hendes fravær og fortalt, at selskabet er brudt op, og Rochester er rejst til London — måske for at købe en vogn til sit bryllup med Blanche.

24.modern-en: Genuinely worried about the engagement between Jane and Rochester. Warns Jane that gentlemen in Rochester's position rarely marry their governesses and urges her to keep her distance until the wedding.
24.modern-da: Oprigtigt bekymret over forlovelsen mellem Jane og Rochester. Advarer Jane om, at herremænd i Rochesters position sjældent gifter sig med deres guvernanter, og opfordrer hende til at holde afstand indtil brylluppet.

26.modern-en: Stands in the hall as Rochester rushes Jane to the church. Watches the wedding party return in disarray. A silent witness to the disaster.
26.modern-da: Står i hallen, da Rochester skynder Jane af sted til kirken. Ser bryllupsselskabet vende tilbage i uorden. Et tavst vidne til katastrofen.

11.modern-en: Appears after the eerie laugh on the third floor — a plain, stocky, red-haired woman of about thirty-five. Mrs. Fairfax tells her to keep the noise down. Jane finds her disappointingly unromantic as a supposed source of the supernatural laughter.
11.modern-da: Dukker op efter den uhyggelige latter på tredje sal — en simpel, kraftig, rødhåret kvinde på omkring femogtredive. Mrs. Fairfax beder hende dæmpe larmen. Jane finder hende skuffende uromantisk som formodet kilde til den overnaturlige latter.

12.modern-en: Jane occasionally sees her carrying trays and beer between the third floor and kitchen. Always taciturn, giving only monosyllabic answers. Jane's attempts at conversation go nowhere.
12.modern-da: Jane ser hende af og til bære bakker og øl mellem tredje sal og køkkenet. Altid fåmælt, giver kun enstavelsesord til svar. Janes forsøg på samtale fører ingensteds hen.

16.modern-en: Blamed for the fire in Rochester's room. Jane is baffled that she remains employed after apparently trying to murder her master. Grace sits calmly sewing, showing no guilt.
16.modern-da: Får skylden for branden i Rochesters værelse. Jane er forvirret over, at hun forbliver ansat, efter tilsyneladende at have forsøgt at myrde sin herre. Grace sidder roligt og syr uden tegn på skyld.

26.modern-en: Found in Bertha's cell, calmly cooking over the fire. Warns Rochester to be careful with his wife. Her role as Bertha's keeper is finally revealed.
26.modern-da: Findes i Berthas celle, hvor hun roligt laver mad over ilden. Advarer Rochester om at være forsigtig med sin hustru. Hendes rolle som Berthas vogterske afsløres endelig.

36.modern-en: The innkeeper explains that Grace's weakness for gin allowed Bertha to steal her keys and set the fatal fire. Her failure of vigilance led to the destruction of Thornfield.
36.modern-da: Kromanden forklarer, at Grace' svaghed for gin tillod Bertha at stjæle hendes nøgler og starte den fatale brand. Hendes svigtende årvågenhed førte til Thornfields ødelæggelse.

16.modern-en: Described by Mrs. Fairfax as tall, dark, and brilliantly beautiful — Rochester's apparent match. Jane paints her portrait from imagination to discipline her own feelings.
16.modern-da: Beskrives af Mrs. Fairfax som høj, mørk og strålende smuk — Rochesters tilsyneladende match. Jane maler hendes portræt efter sin fantasi for at disciplinere sine egne følelser.

17.modern-en: Arrives at Thornfield and dominates the evening. Tall, regal, with dark ringlets and haughty manner. Flirts openly with Rochester, mocks governesses contemptuously, and looks down on Jane. Accomplished but unkind.
17.modern-da: Ankommer til Thornfield og dominerer aftenen. Høj, majestætisk, med mørke lokker og hovmodig fremtoning. Flirter åbenlyst med Rochester, håner guvernanter foragt fuldt og ser ned på Jane. Begavet, men uvenlig.

18.modern-en: Performs in charades with Rochester, playing a bride to his groom. Jane watches in anguish, though she observes that Rochester seems to be performing rather than feeling genuine attraction.
18.modern-da: Optræder i pantomime med Rochester og spiller brud til hans brudgom. Jane ser til i kval, skønt hun bemærker, at Rochester synes at spille skuespil snarere end at føle ægte tiltrækning.

23.modern-en: Rochester reveals to Jane that he never intended to marry Blanche — she was merely a device to provoke Jane's jealousy. Blanche, he says, only wanted his fortune and cooled the moment he hinted at financial difficulty.
23.modern-da: Rochester afslører for Jane, at han aldrig havde til hensigt at gifte sig med Blanche — hun var blot et middel til at provokere Janes jalousi. Blanche, siger han, ville kun have hans formue og kølnedes, da han antydede økonomiske vanskeligheder.

18.modern-en: Arrives unexpectedly at the house party. A pale, mild-mannered stranger from the West Indies. His arrival causes Rochester to turn visibly pale and ask Jane for support.
18.modern-da: Ankommer uventet til selskabet. En bleg, mild fremmed fra Vestindien. Hans ankomst får Rochester til at blegne synligt og bede Jane om støtte.

20.modern-en: Found bleeding and moaning in a third-floor room, attacked by his own sister Bertha. Jane nurses him through the night. Sent away at dawn by Rochester, who extracts a promise of silence. Timid and easily cowed.
20.modern-da: Findes blødende og stønnende i et værelse på tredje sal, angrebet af sin egen søster Bertha. Jane plejer ham natten igennem. Sendes bort ved daggry af Rochester, der aftvinger ham et løfte om tavshed. Frygtsom og let at kue.

26.modern-en: Returns to halt the wedding, testifying that Rochester is already married to his sister Bertha. Trembles before Rochester's fury but stands his ground with the solicitor Briggs at his side.
26.modern-da: Vender tilbage for at standse brylluppet og vidner om, at Rochester allerede er gift med hans søster Bertha. Skælver over for Rochesters raseri, men holder stand med advokaten Briggs ved sin side.

1.modern-en: The nursemaid at Gateshead. Scolds Jane but also shows occasional tenderness. Carries Jane to the red room on Mrs. Reed's orders.
1.modern-da: Barnepigen på Gateshead. Skælder Jane ud, men viser også lejlighedsvis ømhed. Bærer Jane til det røde værelse på Mrs. Reeds ordre.

2.modern-en: Locks Jane in the red room with Abbot. Shows some sympathy but follows Mrs. Reed's orders. Jane feels Bessie is still the kindest person at Gateshead.
2.modern-da: Låser Jane inde i det røde værelse sammen med Abbot. Viser nogen medfølelse, men følger Mrs. Reeds ordrer. Jane føler, at Bessie stadig er den venligste person på Gateshead.

3.modern-en: Tends Jane after her collapse with unusual gentleness. Sings melancholy songs about orphans. Overhears and shares gossip about Jane's parents — that her father was a poor clergyman and both died of typhus.
3.modern-da: Passer Jane efter hendes sammenbrud med usædvanlig mildhed. Synger melankolske sange om forældreløse. Overhører og deler sladder om Janes forældre — at hendes far var en fattig præst, og begge døde af tyfus.

4.modern-en: Serves as an inconsistent but sometimes warm presence during Jane's final months at Gateshead. Has a changeable temper but genuine natural ability. Jane recognizes her as the best person she knew there.
4.modern-da: Fungerer som en ustadig, men til tider varm tilstedeværelse i Janes sidste måneder på Gateshead. Har et omskifteligt temperament, men ægte naturlig begavelse. Jane anerkender hende som den bedste person, hun kendte der.

10.modern-en: Visits Jane at Lowood after eight years. Now married to the coachman Robert Leaven. Tells Jane that the Reeds have fallen on hard times and that Georgiana's London debut was ruined by Eliza's jealousy.
10.modern-da: Besøger Jane på Lowood efter otte år. Nu gift med kusken Robert Leaven. Fortæller Jane, at familien Reed har fået det svært, og at Georgianas London-debut blev ødelagt af Elizas jalousi.

21.modern-en: Sends her husband Robert to fetch Jane to Gateshead when Mrs. Reed is dying. Still loyal to the family, she helps care for the dying woman.
21.modern-da: Sender sin mand Robert for at hente Jane til Gateshead, da Mrs. Reed ligger for døden. Stadig loyal over for familien hjælper hun med at pleje den døende kvinde.
